Home | Halstead St Andrew’s School | An Independent School in Surrey | Prep-School | Ages 2-13
A well-rounded education
Prep School
From Year 3, pupils enjoy continuing outstanding teaching and at Halstead St Andrew's we are committed to preparing pupils as they continue their educational journey.
Find out more about our Prep School
Welcome to Halstead St Andrew’s
I am filled with a profound sense of honour and excitement to introduce myself as the new Head of Halstead St Andrew’s School, an independent co-educational all-through school in Woking, Surrey. At Halstead St Andrew’s, we are more than just a school; we are a family and it is a privilege to lead this exceptional community. As a family-oriented school, we are dedicated to creating a caring, secure, and nurturing environment where pupils thrive as happy and confident learners. Our values-driven and opportunity-rich ethos provides an inspiring educational experience that fosters the holistic development of every pupil while instilling a lifelong love of learning.​
Our ethos is built on our five core values — Endeavour, Positivity, Creativity, Respect, and Kindness. These values are not just guiding principles; they are the foundation of our daily practice. We believe that a positive mindset, a spirit of determination, and a commitment to kindness are essential in preparing our pupils to navigate an ever-changing world.
I warmly invite you to visit our school to experience first hand the vibrant and supportive community we have cultivated. A personal tour will give you the opportunity to see our vision in action, meet our dedicated staff, see our superb facilities, and witness the enthusiasm and joy of our pupils. I look forward to welcoming you and your family to Halstead St Andrew’s, where every child is encouraged to reach their full potential in a happy, nurturing, and inspiring environment.
Admissions
A warm welcome awaits at Halstead St Andrew’s
We know that choosing the right school for your child is a big decision for you as a family. The best way to truly understand what makes Halstead St Andrew’s so special is to visit us in person. We are a warm, family-orientated school where every child is known and valued - and we’d love to show you what life here is really like.
Start your journey with HSA here
Beyond the Classroom
BEYOND THE CLASSROOM
We believe that a well-rounded education extends beyond the classroom. That’s why we offer a wide range of carefully planned extracurricular opportunities designed to inspire curiosity, build confidence, and support your child’s individual journey.
Head's Welcome
At Halstead St Andrew’s, we believe that a truly great school is one where every pupil feels known, valued and inspired to be their best, not just academically, but as a person.
As Head, it is a privilege to lead a school where pupils are not only encouraged to aim high, but are supported every step of the way by dedicated staff, strong values, and a genuine sense of family. We are proud to be a co-educational school in the heart of Woking, Surrey. We are a school where kindness matters, individuality is celebrated, and children grow in confidence as they move through each stage of their educational journey.
Pre-Prep
Halstead St Andrew's Early Years Foundation Stage consists of our Nursery, Rising Reception and Reception classes. Here, we nurture and encourage all of our children to develop a love of school that will form a firm foundation for their future happiness and success.
Find out more about Pre-Prep
Visit Us
You don't need to wait for an Open event to visit. Book a personal tour with us when its convient for you and your family.
Book a personal tour
An environment where every child can thrive
A happy beginning for bright futures
At Halstead St Andrew’s we nurture each child in a safe, caring environment where kindness, curiosity and confidence flourish. Led by experienced staff, we inspire a lifelong love of learning while supporting every child’s unique potential.
A happy beginning for bright futures — rooted in respect, warmth and encouragement.
A perfect start to our child's early learning journey!
A thriving environment
Kindness and respect are at the heart of all we do
We take pride in helping children grow into well-mannered, enthusiastic learners who are curious about the world and confident in who they are. We work closely with each child, nurturing their individual strengths, encouraging positivity, and helping them develop important social and emotional skills.
A really nurturing environment where the children learn primarily through play, with a gradual introduction of structure to prepare them for Reception.
A well-rounded education
We strive to give pupils the foundations to grow in confidence
Joining Pre-School is a special milestone, and at Halstead St Andrew’s, we make the transition as smooth and reassuring as possible. Our dedicated team focuses on the wellbeing and happiness of every child, ensuring they feel safe, supported and excited to begin their learning journey.
A well-rounded journey
Our focus is always on building self-esteem, kindness and curiosity
We believe children thrive when they are recognised and celebrated.
At Halstead St Andrew’s, we create a positive, uplifting environment where children feel happy, supported and proud of who they are. It’s a joyful beginning to a lifelong journey of learning and growth.
Our caring, supportive community and continues throughout their entire learning journey with us
A well-rounded education
We strive to inspire every child to be confident
We understand that choosing the right school for your child is important.
We like to encourage our families to book a personal visit for the opportunity to find out more about our school, teachers and life at Halstead St Andrew's.
If you would like to book a personal tour, please complete the 'Register Your Interest' form, and we will be in touch to organise a personal tour with our Head at your convenience or a video meeting.
We encourage every pupil to give their best
The success of Halstead St Andrew’s School is built upon our values of endeavour, positivity, creativity, respect and kindness. These values form the foundation of everything that we do from the moment your child joins HSA.
Find out more about our school by booking a visit.
We offer personalised mentorship that supports every pupil
We support pupils in unlocking their full potential
Our inclusive, individualised approach means each pupil is supported to thrive - academically and personally - at their own pace. Mentorship across year groups strengthens this, offering pupils the chance to guide, inspire, and learn from one another. It’s through these relationships that confidence grows, interests deepen and critical thinking is nurtured.
A close-knit, supportive community
Guided by values, grounded in care
At the heart of HSA is a thriving, nurturing community where pupils grow into confident, well-rounded individuals
The school’s ethos is rooted in strong values that ensure every child feels supported, celebrated, and inspired to develop a lifelong love of learning. Our five core values; endeavour, positivity, creativity, respect and kindness underpin every lesson, interaction and achievement from the moment your child joins HSA.
These values are brought to life through a rich academic curriculum, exciting co-curricular opportunities and a strong House system that promotes leadership, mentorship and belonging.
For parents wanting the personal touch, this school delivers
Your future starts here
A thriving, nurturing community
From the moment your child joins Halstead St Andrew's, we're committed to your child's education. Our values-driven approach starts from Nursery and continues during their entire educational journey with us until Year 8.
More than just academics
Preparing for life beyond the classroom
At Halstead St Andrew’s, we know that choosing a school is about more than academics — it’s about finding a caring, family-focused community where your child can truly grow and thrive.
We believe in an education that goes far beyond the classroom. That’s why we offer a rich variety of thoughtfully designed extracurricular activities, each aimed at sparking curiosity, building confidence and supporting your child’s unique path.
We offer a well-rounded education
With more than 200 years of Prep School excellence, HSA is grounded in strong values and committed to empowering every child to become a confident, compassionate and curious learner with a lifelong love of learning.
From Nursery through to Year 8, HSA is dedicated to guiding each child’s journey with a values-led approach from day one. With innovative teaching and outstanding pastoral care, pupils are prepared not only for academic achievement but also for life in a changing world.
Academic
We have designed our curriculum to bring the best out of all our pupils, ensuring the pupils are prepared to take the next stage in their educational journey. As part of that journey, Halstead St Andrew's will prepare your child for that next step beyond Year 8.
Beyond the classroom
We offer a wide range of carefully planned extracurricular opportunities designed to inspire curiosity, build confidence, and support your child’s individual journey.
Pastoral and Wellbeing
Together with our dedicated and qualified pastoral team, HSA strives to nurture each child, so they feel supported, valued and safe as they navigate through their school years.

Inspection Reports
Halstead St Andrew's is inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI).
We're thrilled to announce that Halstead St Andrew's met all the standards in all areas during an inpection in May 2026 by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI), an organisation responsible for the inspection of independent schools across England.
Mr Ward commented: "This report captures the very essence of Halstead St Andrew's. It recognises the warmth, ambition and inclusivity that define our school, whilst celebrating the exceptional commitment of our staff and the remarkable character of our pupils. I could not be prouder of our whole community."
Read the ISI Report in full here
Schools are judged on eight key aspects: the quality of pupils’ achievements and learning; the contribution of curricular and extra-curricular provision; the contribution of teaching; the pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development; the contribution of arrangements for pastoral care; the contribution of arrangements for welfare, health and safety; the quality of governance, and the quality of leadership and management, including links with parents, carers and guardians.

Halstead St Andrew's School | An Independent school in Woking, Surrey | Nursery and Rising Reception
Nursery to Reception
Foundation Stage
Halstead St Andrew's Early Years Foundation Stage consists of Nursery, Rising Reception and Reception classes. Here, we nurture and encourage all our children to develop a love of school that will form a firm foundation for their future happiness and success. Both Ofsted and the Independent Schools Inspectorate have rated our Early Years as “Outstanding”.
We are acutely aware that pupils enter the foundation stage at a variety of stages both in maturity and academic ability. Children learn in different ways and progression in their learning happens at their own pace. We cater for children’s individual needs within each area of the curriculum, building on their existing understanding and experiences.
Providing a broad and balanced curriculum across the three Prime and four Specific areas of learning as defined by the statutory Early Years Foundation Stage, we also add that little extra ingredient that is special to our school. Teaching and learning is lively and stimulating, much of it outdoors, with a mixture of self-initiated experiences and adult planned instructions.
We place a great emphasis on Literacy and Numeracy right from the start whilst still ensuring that our children have the opportunity to be creative and imaginative thinkers and explorers.
Children benefit from bright and colourful purpose-built classrooms. The extensive resources are presented imaginatively to motivate children’s interests and learning opportunities both inside and outside.
Nursery
Our Nursery is a very happy, vibrant place where children feel secure and gain independence. Every day there are wonderful things to do and to learn. Nursery promotes enquiring minds and equips children with the skills, knowledge and positive attitudes that are all key to their future success. Specialist lessons in PE, outdoor learning, music and drama, enhance the children experiences.
Why not join us for a Stay & Play session at HSA. It's a perfect opportunity to see our nursery setting in action. Book a session today.
Rising Reception
Children develop their early phonics and numeracy skills in fun and lively ways so that they are ideally prepared for transition into their Reception class. Specialist lessons in PE, outdoor learning, music and drama, enhance the children experiences.
Our Rising Reception is a very happy, vibrant place where children feel secure and gain independence. Every day there are wonderful things to do and to learn.
Reception
Children have many opportunities to experiment, discover, understand and develop as they relish learning to read, write and understand numbers. Children continue to develop good relationships and respect for others. The Reception teachers build on and extend the work already done in the Nursery and Rising Reception. They continue to enhance their literacy and numeracy skills in fun practical ways. Children’s artistic and creative abilities are further enhanced by the provision of specialist teachers in music, French, PE, outdoor learning and dance.
Throughout the school year our children have the opportunity to take part in a range of special events including meeting visiting speakers, outings, charity days, theme weeks and sports day.
The Early Years Foundation Stage is just the beginning of a child’s learning journey at Halstead St Andrew’s. This level of care and commitment is maintained throughout the school.
The transitions between our Foundation Stage, Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 are well planned for and sensitively managed so that our children always move smoothly on to their next stage in learning.
Visit us when it suits you. Book a personal tour.

Board of Governors | Halstead St Andrew's, Woking
Board of Governors
Appointed at St. Andrew's in April 2017
Lukas was born in the Czech Republic, and moved to England in 1998 where he completed A Levels, undergraduate studies and gained an MBA at the University of Durham. He has been teaching Economics and Business at Reed’s School since 2006, was a resident boarding tutor and a Housemaster before becoming an Assistant Head with responsibility for the Middle School (Y9-Y11) in September 2016. Lukas is responsible for introducing Mindfulness and the .b Foundations course to Reed’s and continues to be involved in the Combined Cadet Force, Careers and rugby.
In his spare time, he is passionate about ice hockey, enjoys tennis and spending time with family. He is married to Emma, a teacher of Classics, and they have two young boys, Jonny and Billy. Lukas is the specialist Governor for Safeguarding.
Mr Lukas Pytel can be contacted c/o the school: Halstead St Andrew's School Trust, Church Hill House, Wilson Way, Horsell, Woking, Surrey GU21 4QW.
Bursary (Chair) and Finance & General Purposes (FGP) Committees Appointed at Halstead in March 2016
Simon Hartley has been a solicitor for over 30 years and a partner at Norton Rose Fulbright LLP for over 20 years. He has two daughters, both of whom attended Halstead.
Early Years Governor, Finance & General Purposes (FGP) and Pastoral, Education & Staffing Committees Appointed at Halstead in July 2022
Beryl Hunwicks is a retired deputy head teacher, having had 35 years’ experience in Senior State and Private Prep School Education as well as overseeing and marking overseas O Level Examinations. She gained further qualifications as an ESOL teacher and taught locally for seven years in that capacity. Beryl has served in Local Government for 14 years, making and developing strategies for the communities in Woking.
She became Mayor of Woking in 2019 and served for two years, allowing her to learn about and meet many wonderful charities in the Borough. She now serves as a Member of The Swan Trust, is Chairman of The Maybury Centre Trustees, is a Trustee of The Friends of Woking Community Hospital and Community Links Coordinator for CAP (Christians Against Poverty) at Welcome Church.
Vice Chair of Governors Appointed at Halstead in October 2018
Faith has over 25 years' experience in the risk and insurance industry and is a Chartered Insurer. Faith was appointed Head of Client Relationship Management for Allianz in 2024 and works closely with a number of sectors, including the education sector, the heritage sector and the charitable sector in her role. She is also a qualified counsellor and runs her own private practice, specialising in providing therapy to young people and young adults.
Finance & General Purposes (FGP), Health & Safety Appointed to Halstead St Andrew's in January 2026
Ian McKissock was born in Scotland and raised in Sydney, Australia. He recently retired after a 41-year career in the global oil industry, having held senior leadership roles with BP, Mobil, and ExxonMobil. His professional background spans research, operations, and supply chain management, with a strong emphasis on operational excellence, customer service, and the highest standards of health and safety.
Ian’s career was predominantly international, with leadership roles in Sweden, Belgium, Germany, and Singapore. He brings significant global experience, strategic insight, and a disciplined approach to governance, which he is keen to apply in support of the school’s long-term development and success. Ian and his wife, Antonia, have two adult daughters, and the family has a strong connection to the school, with two grandchildren currently attending Halstead St Andrew's. His personal interests include travel and gliding, reflecting his curiosity, resilience, and lifelong passion for learning.
Chair of Finance and General Purposes Appointed at Halstead St Andrew's in January 2026
Julian has been a Chartered Accountant for the last 25 years and has been head of the UK office of Saltgate for the last 7 years. Julian has 2 sons both of whom attended Halstead St. Andrew’s and he lives with his family in Woking.

Uniform
Uniform
Full uniform must be worn at all times when on the school grounds.
All uniform, kit and equipment for the appropriate term is required in school from the first day of term and should be labelled, including footwear. All children should have a named water bottle in school.
Please refer to the document below for your child's school-year uniform.
Sports Kit All pupils are expected to wear the HSA sports kit which is part of the compulsory uniform.
Hair should be worn in a neat and manageable style. No hair colouring is permitted. Shoulder-length or longer hair must be tied back, and short hair must not touch the collar or fall below the eyebrows.
No extreme hairstyles are permitted. In accordance with the HALO code, we support culturally significant hairstyles. Hair wraps, scarves and accessories should be a plain dark colour. Please speak to the school if you require more clarification.
The only jewellery pupils are allowed to wear are a traditional wristwatch (no smartwatches) and a pair of small stud earrings. No other jewellery of any kind is permitted unless on medical/religious grounds. Permitted jewellery must be removed for Physical Education lessons - swimming, games, gymnastics or dancing.
Earrings cannot be taped over indefinitely, and it is both a school and IAPS policy that all jewellery must be removed for competitive games. Pupils will not be able to participate in fixtures against any schools whilst wearing any jewellery.
All items will be available to purchase via our dedicated store on SchoolBlazer.com
The Schoolblazer online shop clearly identifies which items are compulsory and must be purchased directly through Schoolblazer, as well as those items which are optional or may be sourced elsewhere. We are also pleased to let you know that Schoolblazer will be offering a free delivery period from 29th June to 12th July.
Buy your uniform from Schoolblazer
We would also politely request that children wear plain black or navy school shoes or trainers.
Our PTA, Friends of Halstead St Andrew’s (FOHSA) run a second-hand uniform shop (known as Swap Shop) on Friday mornings 08:00-09:00 term time. Please do pop along and meet the team, they are very helpful. If you have any questions regards Swap Shop or stock levels, please email swapshop@friendsofhsa.com
As well as selling second hand uniform, Swap Shop also carries samples of several key pieces of uniform in the full range of sizes so that parents can check sizing before ordering new items from School Blazer.

Start your Journey
A Warm Welcome Awaits at Halstead St Andrew’s
At Halstead St Andrew’s, we understand that choosing the right school is one of the most important decisions you’ll make for your child. From your first visit to your first day, you’ll find a nurturing, inclusive environment where every child is known, valued, and encouraged to thrive. Our admissions team is here to support you at every step of the journey.
Contact the Admission team
Discover what makes us different
We believe that the best way to get a true feel for life at Halstead St Andrew’s is to experience it in person. From our vibrant classrooms and dedicated teachers to the laughter in the playground and the calm focus of our learning spaces, every visit tells a story of care, curiosity, and character. We invite you to explore our school and see how we inspire confidence and joy in every child.
Register for our Open Day
What to expect from our admissions process
We know the admissions process can feel overwhelming — that’s why we’re here to guide you every step of the way. Whether you're joining in Nursery, Reception or further up the school, our admissions team ensures a clear, personal experience tailored to your child’s journey.
We welcome you to get in touch with our admissions team to express your interest and ask any initial questions. We’re here to listen and help you explore whether Halstead St Andrew’s is the right fit for your child.
Step Two: Visit and Tour
Experience our warm community first-hand with a personal tour or by attending one of our Open Mornings. You’ll meet our Head, explore our facilities, and see the school in action.
Step Three: Taster Day
To help your child settle in and feel at ease, we invite them to spend a taster day with us. It’s a chance for them to meet their potential classmates and teachers, and to experience the rhythm of a typical day at Halstead.
Arrange a Taster Day
Step Four: Registration
If you would like to proceed, we’ll ask you to complete a short registration form and pay a registration fee. This officially places your child on our admissions list for the relevant year group.
Step Five: Offer and Acceptance
Following the taster day, and depending on availability, we will make a formal offer of a place. Once you accept and return the acceptance form with the deposit, your child’s place is confirmed.
Step Six: Welcome to Halstead
We’ll stay in close contact in the lead-up to your child’s first day. You’ll receive a welcome pack with everything you need to know — and our staff will be on hand to ensure your family feels fully supported as you join our community.

Planning for your child’s education is an important step, and our fee calculator is here to help. Simply select your child’s year group and any additional options to receive an instant estimate tailored to your family’s needs. It’s quick, easy, and designed to give you a clear picture of what to expect.

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior school collaboration with Effingham Schools Trust | Prep Schools in Surrey | Independent Schools in Woking | Halstead St Andrew's, Woking
pageCache.text:
Senior school collaboration with Effingham Schools Trust | Prep Schools in Surrey | Independent Schools in Woking | Halstead St Andrew's, Woking
Senior school collaboration
The collaboration, announced in March, will strengthen senior school pathways for pupils beyond Year 8 and brings together HSA with Cranmore and St Teresa’s, two highly regarded senior schools within EST.
The move will create a clear and supportive progression route for pupils through to age 18 while preserving the distinctive identity and independence of each school.
The collaboration aligns schools that share a commitment to outstanding academic standards, exceptional pastoral care and a values-driven approach to education.
The agreed collaboration between HSA and EST ensures that each school retains its governance, admissions processes, fee structures, ethos and school identity.
Both HSA and EST both strongly believe that Year 7 and 8 prep school education gives pupils both academic and leadership skills to best prepare them for Year 9 and beyond.
The collaboration provides HSA pupils with a defined pathway into Year 9 at Cranmore or St Teresa’s, while the school will continue to prepare pupils for the 11+ and support families in choosing from a wide range of Senior school destinations.
What this means for your child
The Pathway refers specifically to Year 9 entry, offering students a structured route into Effingham Schools Trust at this stage of their education.
Students applying for Year 7 entry will continue to follow the standard EST admissions process, ensuring consistency and fairness for all applicants.
Students on the Pathway will benefit from access to EST’s high-quality facilities and resources, supporting both their academic progress and wider development.
Students on the Pathway will be offered a guaranteed place at EST, subject to meeting the agreed requirements. This provides reassurance and continuity for families planning ahead.
There is no 11+ examination requirement for students entering via the Pathway, reducing pressure and making the transition more accessible.
As part of the process, students will attend an interview, allowing the school to get to know each individual and ensure the Pathway is the right fit.
Applications for students with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) will be considered in line with statutory guidance, ensuring appropriate support and provision are in place.
Bursaries awarded at HSA will be honoured into Year 9 at EST. From Year 10 onwards, bursaries will be externally means tested
Scholarships awarded at HSA will be honoured into Year 9. EST scholarships will continue for the duration of a pupils time at EST
From September 2027, a dedicated HSA direct minibus service will run each day from the HSA site
A discounted rate will apply for HSA pupils
Pupils will also have the flexibility to use any EST minibus service
A late bus service (Lion Retail) will be available to support pupils attending after-school activities
Sibling discounts will be on offer for HSA pupils

Alumni success: Former pupil wins second place at cheer competition | Halstead St Andrew’s | Independent School Woking | Prep Schools in Woking
Former HSA pupil success at international Cheer competition
A former pupil has achieved international success after competing at one of the world’s most prestigious youth cheerleading events.
Abi C travelled to Orlando, Florida, during the Easter break to take part in the Prep and Rec Grand Nationals, a major competition that attracts top young athletes from across the globe. Representing the Diamonds squad — part of the AllStar cheerleading club based near Cobham, Surrey — Abi and her teammates had earned their place at the event after qualifying for their first overseas competition last year.
Facing strong international competition, the team delivered an impressive performance, finishing second in their division. Abi’s category featured 14 teams, highlighting the scale and competitiveness of the event.
Abi’s club has previously described the competition as the pinnacle of achievement for prep-level cheerleaders, and one of the most decorated events available to athletes of this age group.
Congratulations to Abi and her team.

pageCache.pageTitle: Halstead St Andrew’s to move entire school to one site | Halstead St Andrew’s | Independent School Woking | Prep Schools in Woking
pageCache.text:
Halstead St Andrew’s to move entire school to one site | Halstead St Andrew’s | Independent School Woking | Prep Schools in Woking
HSA to move to one site
Halstead St Andrew’s has announced from January 2026, the whole school will be based on its Church Hill House site.
Pupils from Nursery to Year 2 will join those from Years 3–8 on one site, enabling the school to continue to invest in high quality teaching, learning, and facilities for all pupils.
The expansion of the Senior school, into Year 9, will also be delayed until September 2027. This is due to the extremely small cohort currently in Year 8 and the financial viability of running this year group in the future.
Andrew Ward, Head, said: "This change brings the whole school community together on one site, providing greater shared experiences for all pupils, and much simpler logistics for parents and the school alike. By aligning our structure now, we can continue to provide the very best opportunities for every child.”
The move will also bring other benefits too, including a new whole-school mentoring programme with more opportunities for younger pupils to learn from older role models. Outdoor play equipment will be relocated to Church Hill House and Pre-Prep pupils will benefit from greater access to subject specialist staff.
Mr Ward added: “We are not immune from the economic challenges facing all independent schools, with some schools closing or changing their models. However, this proactive step will help us build a strong and sustainable future for HSA. We are confident that Halstead St Andrew’s has a bright future ahead.
"The facilities at Church Hill House will be adapted to accommodate all pupils, and parents will be updated regularly as plans progress.”

pageCache.pageTitle: HSA has a 'nurturing culture that prioritises pupils’ wellbeing', says ISI | Halstead St Andrew’s | Independent School Woking | Prep Schools in Woking
pageCache.text:
HSA has a 'nurturing culture that prioritises pupils’ wellbeing', says ISI | Halstead St Andrew’s | Independent School Woking | Prep Schools in Woking
HSA has a 'nurturing culture that prioritises pupils’ wellbeing', says ISI Report
Following on from an inspection by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) in May 2026, Halstead St Andrew's School is thrilled to announce the school met all the standards in all areas.
The report highlighted key strengths, particularly the school's nurturing culture, strong pastoral care, excellent academic outcomes, community ethos, broad curriculum, early years provision, and successful senior school destinations.
The report also noted that Halstead St Andrew's provides a "collaborative, nurturing culture", pupils "typically secure places at their senior school of choice, with many receiving scholarships and exhibitions", and that children thrive in a supportive, engaging environment.
Below are some of the highlights from the ISI Report:
“The school’s inclusive ethos is reflected in its effective pastoral support, which ensures that pupils feel valued and included.”
“Leaders foster a collaborative, nurturing culture that prioritises pupils’ wellbeing.”
"The curriculum is age-appropriate, inclusive and underpinned by high aspirations for pupils."
“Children in the early years benefit from engaging activities that nurture their emotional wellbeing.”
“Teachers and teaching assistants create a calm, well-managed environment and maintain positive relationships with pupils, encouring them to contribute and engage with learning confidently.”
Mr Ward commented: "This report captures the very essence of Halstead St Andrew's. It recognises the warmth, ambition and inclusivity that define our school, whilst celebrating the exceptional commitment of our staff and the remarkable character of our pupils. I could not be prouder of our whole community."
